(Top) Generation of chords for the LCO phase (blue vectors) and the combined interparticle phase (green vectors): 26 vectors are projected in angularly equispaced directions from random seed points until they hit an interface (the figure shows exemplarily vectors in the xy-plane). A pair of opposing vectors is combined to one chord. Chords hitting the image border (cf. dashed red line) are rejected. (Bottom) µ- and k-values for LCO, SE, and void phases as well as the combined interparticle phase from CLD analysis, with stepwise increase of the investigated sample volume to address finite-size effects.

figures.caption: Fig. 4. Reconstruction process for a single slice of the composite cathode (all scale bars: 15 μm). (A) Image after restoration process. (B) LCO phase (white) after finished reconstruction. (C) Void space (white) combining the resin-filled volume and residual void volume. (D) Final image combining the three reconstructed phases: blue – LCO particles; red – SE; black – void space. SE was assigned as volume neither occupied by LCO nor void phase.

figures.caption: Fig. 6. (A) Phase distribution in an individual slice of the reconstructed cathode. SE is shown in red. Black represents LCO particles and void space, which are both unavailable for diffusion of ions. The SE volume fraction is 53.7% (cf. Table 3). (B) Same slice, but voids are now filled with SE. Therefore, black represents only the LCO particles (cf. Fig. 4B) and the SE volume fraction has increased to 66.9%. Scale bar: 15 μm.
